# W13 current W11 endpoint profile

One authorized diagnostic run of current W11-equivalent code completed with **15,235 decompiler-worker endpoints**,81 caller endpoints, and all **51 × 3,350 = 170,850** locked source-hash comparisons passing. This is wall-stack endpoint evidence selected by prior thread CPU progress, **not on-CPU sampling, CPU percentages, or an ordinary speed benchmark**. No threshold-chasing rerun occurred.

## Reproducibility and capture quality

- Child PID9868 ran from 2026-09-27T22:24:24.579406+00:00 to 2026-09-27T22:30:58.130433+00:00; wrapper finished 2026-09-27T22:31:01.549115+00:00. One Rayon worker, affinity8388608, requested10ms jittered delay, fixed50 recomputations plus first call,600s cap; no timeout.
- Frozen W11 source530files matched before/after build and after capture. Current702075a differs from6bbdcc1 only in performance documents. Default features, matched full package graph, release optimization, local debug=2 and strip=false; mimalloc global DEBUG remained false. Native allocator code/data/relocations/symbol tables match ordinary W11 after excluding only metadata. Build356.76s is build duration, not runtime.
- API EXE `0f52afabec0046bd08e27e523064c2d0cddfa00d3b4c5bb71db0b77c577d05f4`; matching PDB `b46ae6bc8e101fa5d98f24b84fe3506265446eb86ca95963d443715266b21f18`. PE/PDB GUID+age checked. The sampler source/binary/PDB and both workflow scripts exactly match validated W5 pins.
- All15316 successful suspensions have matching resumes. There were68 pre-capture failures; existing code does not separately log OpenThread/owner-check versus CPU/cycle-query failures, so their exact cause is unknown. No logged suspend/context errors, denied unwind reads, depth caps or active one-frame stacks. There were662 worker unwind soft-time caps (662 total), so inclusive outer callers can be undercounted.
- Worker interval median29.793ms,p9532.064ms,p99108.686ms,max825.422ms. Pause median74.1us,p95195.4us,p991.671ms,maximum718.752ms; total3.115s,223 above1ms,26 above10ms. Toolhelp inventory cost28.413s in the sampler. Pause cost alone does not bound profiler interference.
- Own-module symbol coverage is complete:0unknown/285569 frame occurrences. System DLL frames remain unresolved, including243 VCRUNTIME140 leaf observations across all threads; do not silently label those as memcpy or algorithm work. Full module counts retained. CPU-delta accounting99.817% and temporal window99.953% are coverage diagnostics, not proof of stack attribution.

## Recurrent costs

The following are **disjoint self-leaf endpoint counts** out of15,235; no CPU share is inferred:

| Primitive family | Endpoints |
|---|---:|
| allocator |1521|
| map/set/hash |1306|
| LocalRw local-read/write visitors |866|
| drop |575|
| child/local Vec selectors |315|
| formatting |279|
| clone |191|

Remaining leaves include other AST passes4386,SSA2605,lifter/pipeline670,naming645,restructure459,and runtime/system/uncategorized1417. These broad buckets include inlined work not exposed as separate symbols.

Largest exact leaf symbols: mi_malloc_aligned770; RValue::visit_local_reads561; SSA Inliner::inline_rvalues327; mi_bitmap_try_find_and_claim304; mi_free303; SSA construct287. Statement::visit_local_reads contributes136 and mutable RValue local reads101. LocalRw appears somewhere in1982 worker stacks counted once per stack; this union is **inclusive and overlaps** all leaf categories above.

Visitor-leaf nearest distinct owned callers span temp usage collection128,SSA inline87,SubtreeUsage85,StatementFacts84,SSA inline_rvalues73,and apply_local_map68. Map/set leaves similarly recur under SSA write_local94,usage callback87,SSA inline callback71,reserved-name insertion66,and liveness62. Allocator nearest callers are dispersed: RValue child-Vec API86,SSA inline74,decompile_function69,stmt_rvalues56,cleanup_ssa50,destructor41. One allocator site cannot explain a several-fold engine gain.

A separate exact-method view has719 Traverse self leaves, already included in broader AST/restructure buckets. Most are **generic recursive** post-walks: inline nested closures75,table-rebuild nested closures66,reserved identifiers48,cleanup_returns nested closures43,dropped-connection traversal33. Direct visit_rvalues_mut is11. This supports investigating repeated descendant scans and shared scope-correct facts, not attributing all719 observations to dyn callbacks.

Across four equal elapsed-time segments (3804/3762/3825/3844 endpoints), LocalRw counts204/196/240/226,map/set334/327/316/329,and allocator400/396/360/365 recur. Broad ordering also persists when excluding unwind-capped samples or pauses above1ms. This is a consistency check only; endpoints remain dependent and sampling bias remains.

## What a generic-visitor pilot can and cannot establish

Source has dyn FnMut low-level LocalRw sinks, while enum_dispatch is a static enum match and recursive Traverse wrappers already generic. Current endpoints identify a concrete shared boundary worth a bounded exact-equivalence experiment. They do **not** isolate vtable-call cost from enum branches, callback work, recursive memory accesses, ownership operations, or facts/map updates. FatLTO may already devirtualize some call sites. No sampled instruction disassembly or indirect-branch evidence was collected, and no inline frames were expanded.

A generic visitor pilot must be judged by matched ordinary end-to-end timing and unchanged output/owner/order/early-exit behavior, with binary-size/codegen effects retained. Alternatively, reuse scope-correct per-function facts or explicit child-function lists to remove repeated walks; this addresses traversal plus collection construction together. The data supports systemic experiments but establishes neither a dominant removable hotspot nor a3x claim.

Input decode, Rayon pool creation, hashing and caller result disposal are outside the API benchmark's own timer but inside process observation. The driver has no separate warmup: round0 is first call, followed by50 recomputations. Stack/thread grouping distinguishes much of setup/caller work, not exact phase windows. Diagnostic per-round elapsed times stay in raw benchmark.json and are excluded from conclusions.

Artifacts: `C:\Users\ADMIN\.codex\tmp\medal-ultra-wave13`. Raw immutable capture is `process-w11-capture-01`; detailed ordered-symbol/caller review `process-w11-review.json`; reproducible family classifier `group_w11_endpoints.py` and `process-w11-families.json`; selector detail `traverse-leaf-detail.json`; pinned native archives `native-allocator-proof`. # W13 constructor copy-shell census

Diagnostic-only source fork from702075a, at C:/Users/ADMIN/.codex/tmp/medal-ultra-20260927-wave13-copy-shell-work. Main untouched. Feature `luau-lifter/copy-shell-census` forwards only to `cfg/copy-shell-census`; no allocator or node-tree instrumentation is enabled. No build/test has been run at source-ready time.

Candidate predicate is exactly Assign with one LValue::Local destination and one RHS. Prefix/parallel flags are counted separately, never interpreted or changed. RHS taxonomy is the13 outer RValue variants. Input records original kinds; constructor only aliases Local operands, so candidate kind and operand-vector capacities remain unchanged outside deletions. Counts contain no expression recursion, pointer/identity maps, AST handles, custom TLS or global state. Three fixed-size numeric snapshots live with one constructor.

Hooks: input before unreachable pruning; pruned snapshot immediately before the existing remove_block; actual copy removal only inside propagate_copies after original capture/source-binding guards; post snapshot after final apply_pending_local_map, before any SSA cleanup/inlining/destruction. Preexisting Empty and CLOSE counts are separate so statement loss cannot be misattributed to copy elision.

Emitted phases are SSA_COPY_SHELL_INPUT, SSA_COPY_SHELL_UNREACHABLE, SSA_COPY_SHELL_REMOVED, SSA_COPY_SHELL_POST_CONSTRUCT, SSA_COPY_SHELL_ACCOUNTING. Standard script/prototype context is inherited. Snapshots sum blocks/statements/Empty/CLOSE, candidates and flags, left/right Vec lengths/capacities, element payload bytes using actual target size_of, candidate Statement slot bytes, and RHS-kind counts. Zero snapshot counters are omitted; absence means zero. Each snapshot has functions=1; removed.blocks remains0 because its hook observes assignments, not a separate block census.

Accounting compares20 fields: candidate count, prefix/parallel counts, both operand lengths/capacities, and13 RHS kinds. Required identity is INPUT=UNREACHABLE+REMOVED+POST_CONSTRUCT in each field. It emits matched/mismatched and never changes decompilation success. Unreachable pruning and copy removal are independent, not inferred from a total delta. Candidate nonempty operand vectors are2 per candidate; this is a potential buffer count, not an observed allocator-call count. Capacity bytes exclude allocator rounding/headers, block capacity, descendants, shared storage and payload cloning. Statement slot bytes are modeled occupied slots, not freed block allocation bytes.

Two focused tests cover shape rejection, exact capacity counts, NaN-containing payload preservation, prefix/parallel flags, local-owner/ID/metadata neutrality, and actual approved-copy hook with captured-cell source/destination refusals plus unreachable/Empty/CLOSE accounting. Existing constructor algorithms and order are unchanged; no alternate optimization is implemented.

Timing limitation: snapshots are collected in the surrounding constructor span and emitted later at coarse subspans; the subspan durations do not measure scan overhead. All probe timings are diagnostic and excluded from speed conclusions. The probe's purpose is to determine whether the proposed pre-cleanup compact-shell handoff could avoid enough allocation, rather than merely defer it.

Validation still pending root/sole-Cargo coordination: cargo test -p cfg --lib --features copy-shell-census copy_shell_census --locked -j2; then cargo check --workspace --all-targets --features luau-lifter/copy-shell-census --locked -j2. Corpus source hashes remain the accepted original expectations. No fullquality/promotion or performance claim is made.

wave13-ast-research.md.text:
# W13 AST research: reusable occurrence facts with explicit mutation deltas

Date: 2026-09-28. Read-only audit of production at `702075a` (production AST remains W11). No source changes, builds, tests, new diagnostics, or timing runs were performed. W12 is rejected and is not part of this proposal.

## Decision

The strongest concrete remaining AST candidate is **one numeric occurrence ledger reused by adjacent cleanup passes, with explicit mutation deltas and unchanged phase barriers**. Its first useful consumer is the UI rebuild/inlining fixed point, but an isolated UI scheduler is not a multiplier-scale project. Extend only after demonstrating reused work across the adjacent ordinary inliner, conditional reconstruction, UI reconstruction, call-receiver materialization, and alias cleanup.

There is **no evidence supporting 3x** from this AST scope. Even the complete measured diagnostic exposure of the first five passes is only 9.36%; the proposed optimization removes only a subset of that work and adds bookkeeping. A later extension to naming preparation, final cleanup and normalization has a descriptive phase envelope of 17.98%, not an achievable saving. A 3x engine improvement requires removing at least two thirds of ordinary execution time; these data cannot support that claim.

## Concrete repeated work still present

1. `luau-lifter/src/lib.rs:780`, `:789`, `:797`, `:805`, `:815` invoke five ordered passes over the same published chunk tree. Their transformations must remain at these boundaries; this proposal shares analysis, not transformations.
2. `ast/src/inline_temps.rs:90-103` builds full usage, captured/stable-captured and optional numeric facts. `:262-264` builds a separate `SubtreeUsage` index. The ordinary inliner and later UI inliner repeat both preparations.
3. `inline_temps.rs:75-87` reruns the complete rebuild traversal and complete inliner every UI round. `rebuild_table_literals.rs:20-29` recursively visits children and invokes four current-block transformations on each block; `:64-77` rediscovers nested closures from every expression. Each subsequent inlining round rebuilds `SubtreeUsage` from scratch.
4. `conditional_expressions.rs:100-106` collects descendant usage for every candidate-bearing block. `:373-419` rewalks nested structured blocks and closure bodies. Its local scheduler is already incremental; the missing reuse is the input census, not the old restart-after-each-rewrite algorithm.
5. `copy_cleanup.rs:30` builds whole-tree capture facts, then `:50-65` constructs descendant usage and runtime-position indexes for each candidate-bearing block. `:118-138` intentionally has a different runtime scope from the full closure-body usage collector. Parent candidate blocks can rewalk children already processed.
6. This mechanism also remains in later consumers: `cleanup_final.rs:32-50` recollects usage solely to derive captures after child mutation; `canonicalize_branches.rs:28-36,78` does so at function entry; `name_locals.rs:5046-5060` has a phase-local preparation followed by semantic usage collection. These cannot all be naively replaced with one universal query.

## What is already fixed, and must not be counted again

- Ordinary/UI inlining already has an ordered candidate worklist, motion-query indexing and subtree occurrence indexing (`inline_temps.rs:282-340`, `inline_temps/usage.rs:64-116`). W10 already moves accepted initializers instead of deep-cloning them.
- Copy cleanup and conditional reconstruction already update local worklists. Copy cleanup already applies exact two-binding count deltas (`copy_cleanup.rs:95-112`); conditional reconstruction documents its one-read/three-write binder removal invariant (`conditional_expressions.rs:96-99`).
- Naming preparation is already fused. Final name refinement already has incremental bounded propagation and indexed scope reservations.
- Normalization already has an owner-free write-position index with budgeted admission (`normalize_conditions/writes.rs:41-89`). W8 counted **237,707 repeated statement visits avoided**, from **204,996 indexed statements**; this is existing production benefit, not W13 opportunity.
- Deinline/factor outer scheduling is not supported as a target by the corpus: W8 recorded exactly 3,936 outer iterations for 3,936 nonempty inputs; the final factor calls reported zero changes.
- No reducer normality cache or W12 representation rescue is proposed.

## Existing evidence and limits

Source: `wave8-census-profile/report.json`, SHA256 `07335be867cf3c5e798ef5466c6f3677a52ce70343b7bf89ad601da33f8f6853`.

| Stage | Exclusive diagnostic seconds |
|---|---:|
| S_INLINE_TEMPS_1 | 0.2563711 |
| S_COND_EXPRS | 0.0494492 |
| S_REBUILD_TABLES | 0.5679564 |
| S_MATERIALIZE_CALL_RECEIVERS | 0.1449841 |
| S_COPY_CLEANUP | 0.0879636 |
| Five-pass envelope | 1.1067244 |
| S_NAME_LOCALS | 0.5469609 |
| S_CLEANUP_FINAL | 0.1543403 |
| S_NORMALIZE_CONDS | 0.3177487 |
| Extended envelope | 2.1257743 |
| DECOMPILE inclusive | 11.8219389 |

These are diagnostic thread-wall measurements with instrumentation, not ordinary CPU shares. Five-pass/all-work is 9.36%; even removing all five passes would give only a descriptive 1.103x ceiling. The expanded 17.98% envelope gives 1.219x under that impossible zero-cost assumption. Never present either as a forecast. W11 representation changes also mean these W7-era data are historical attribution, not current ordinary timings.

W8 UI counters: 14,299 accepted inlines; 18,186 evaluation-position refusals; 21,365 intervening-statement refusals; 2,464 source-binding refusals; 7,129 expression-role refusals; 63 arity/context refusals. Those **49,207 categorized refusals are attempts, not necessarily distinct candidates**, and do not prove how many attempts were repeated without relevant changes. Ordinary inlining recorded only 149 accepts and 30,698 categorized refusals. These make failed-proof reuse worth measuring, but are not CPU measurements.

There is **no corpus UI-round count in W8/W11 evidence**. The twelve existing `CHAIN_PROBE` rows in `wave9-focused.log` all report exactly **two UI rounds**, for constructor and scalar-method chains of lengths 8/16/32/64/128/256. Thus these probes demonstrate a productive round plus convergence scan, not a deep-round explosion. Their former quadratic accepted-copy work was already removed in W10.

W11 layout/SSA censuses count physical nodes and CFG operations. They do not count repeated AST analysis visits after publication; they cannot fill this gap by multiplying node counts by pass count.

## Minimal pilot contract

Introduce no persistent global cache. A private `CleanupAnalysis` session begins after `recover_methods` and ends before `eliminate_nil`, with explicit adapters for the existing five ordered passes. Store only numeric local IDs, analysis-owned scope/occurrence IDs, counts and flags. Do not retain `RcLocal`, function Arc owners, AST references across mutation, or bare expression addresses.

Use distinct query domains:

- Direct runtime operand reads/writes, including capture operands but excluding closure-body execution.
- Legacy descendant usage, including each closure-body occurrence through the legacy RHS selector.
- Function/structured-block subtrees and capture membership.
- Exact per-block source-order position indexes, refreshed after compaction or permutation.

Do not unify those selectors. In particular, the legacy usage census ignores indexed-LHS closure bodies while mutation traversals can enter them (`inline_temps/usage.rs:160-167`, `normalize_conditions/writes.rs:113-121`).

Mutation adapters report numeric deltas only after the existing approved commit point:

| Producer | Required update/invalidation |
|---|---|
| Accepted temp inline | Remove binder read/write, transfer initializer occurrence ownership within its block; refresh edited destination syntax/effects and affected candidate dependencies. Other occurrence totals stay invariant. |
| Short-circuit reconstruction | Remove binder one-read/three-write entries; move surviving condition/arm occurrences; retire removed branch scopes and reparent surviving closure occurrences. Retain current source-order and three-neighbor retry scheduler. |
| Table reconstruction/sinking | Refresh edited source/destination statements, local-read deletions and declaration-run positions; preserve exact field/SetList evaluation ordering and scalarization. Structured/closure bodies moved inside values require occurrence reparenting. |
| Call-receiver materialization | Insert the minted local's declaration/read and refresh modified expression roots and statement positions; no cache may hide the original allocation/ID order. |
| Copy cleanup | Apply the existing src/dst read/capture transfer, update reverse occurrence sites, and invalidate dependent read/write/capture proofs. Preserve the existing runtime-vs-descendant split. |

For the UI fixed point, keep **round barriers**: all rebuild work in original traversal order, then all inline work in original traversal order. A dirty bit means only that the pass's exact dependencies changed since its previous visit. A rebuilt/edited child marks relevant ancestors; capture or alias changes invalidate all affected scopes. Never turn the loop into an unrestricted mixed rewrite queue, which can change intermediate eligibility and output.

The current UI `MotionFacts` snapshot is deliberately fixed across the entire loop. A more current fact can admit a rewrite the old algorithm refused: retain that exact snapshot, even if the ledger can prove more. Likewise every pass must observe its established pre-pass or per-function snapshot, not an eagerly updated cross-pass view.

## Hard invariants and fallback conditions

- Preserve every eligibility predicate, original traversal/commit order, local minting order, source-name protection, phase boundary, metadata lifecycle and clone/move decision.
- Existing expression width/depth/node budgets are **logical work budgets**. A cache hit cannot make an over-budget proof succeed. Store sufficient proof metadata to reproduce the original bounded answer or fall back; do not simply memoize `true`.
- Preserve full Call flags, scalar/multret adjustment, capture Copy/Ref semantics, NaN rules and diagnostic/provenance mode parity.
- Shared closure/block bodies can mutate through earlier occurrences. Either maintain an occurrence graph plus reverse invalidation edges, or refuse indexing for the whole session and use the unchanged legacy path. The minimal pilot should use the latter, like `SubtreeUsage`.
- Reused AST addresses after drop are not identities. Explicit session IDs and generations are necessary; unknown structural mutations invalidate before any lookup, never afterward.
- All caches are owner-free and dropped before later owner-sensitive naming or cleanup. No additional local Arc can reach `name_locals`' unused-local decision.
- Canonicalization's `unshare_blocks`, terminal-return restructuring, and final cleanup's child-first shared-body publication are reset boundaries for an initial pilot. Extending past them needs separate adapters, not an optimistic version bump on the root.

## Falsifiable screen before implementation

If root chooses this direction, a bounded diagnostic can count at existing analysis/walk sites (without adding an extra traversal): physical statement/expression visits, function/block revisits, UI rounds, unchanged rejected-candidate revisits, and successful edits by producer. Aggregate by script and pass; count separately the new ledger setup/update work and conservative fallback frequency. Existing counters do not provide these values.

Proceed to a prototype only if **the same removable mechanism spans a substantial part of multiple stages**, rather than an isolated second UI scan. Retain independent old collectors/schedulers as test oracles; compare exact source, stable local identity relationships, full origin fields and hidden Call flags in ordinary/provenance modes. Then run one frozen ordinary paired cohort. No promotion on operation counts alone.

## Secondary candidate, not recommended yet

A typed naming event stream could reuse syntax discovery across `NamingPreparation`, `gather_usage`, `Namer::collect`, and call-site consensus (`name_locals.rs:5046-5119`, `:3819-3845`). It could replace repeated child/closure discovery and locks while retaining serial hint resolution. But naming already performs important phase-dependent reads, and `Namer::collect` consults current local names and function contexts. There is no per-subwalk timing or occurrence census establishing a large remaining cost; the whole phase is only 0.547 diagnostic seconds. Do not build a generic event framework on this evidence alone.

The practical conclusion is to test the **cross-pass occurrence-ledger hypothesis**, not to promise a multiplier or start another isolated micro-optimization wave. Its main blocker is demonstrating enough actual unchanged work after current worklists and indexes, then preserving their different snapshot/scope semantics cheaply.

wave13-cfg-research.md.text:
# W13 CFG architecture review — read-only

Baseline: main `702075a` documentation over W11 code `6bbdcc1`. No implementation, new census, build, test, or benchmark was run. Source callsites below refer to that main tree. W12 D is rejected; do not carry its boxed RValue representation into another prototype.

## Recommendation

The strongest broad direction is a **private compact instruction/value IR with explicit def-use links and delayed AST materialization**, spanning lifting and SSA cleanup. A narrower direct-SSA emitter or another sparse block scheduler does not have enough demonstrated exposure. This is a substantial alternative backend, not a small optimization ready for promotion. Existing data supports a bounded prototype decision, not a promised 3x gain.

A second, more speculative architecture is an **SSA-aware region planner with delayed edge-copy lowering**. It could remove a conversion boundary, but has stricter output/provenance risks and less convincing measured opportunity. Do not start both simultaneously.

## 1. Compact register/value IR through SSA cleanup

### Work currently performed

* `luau-lifter/src/lifter.rs:165–176` decodes blocks in reverse PC order into complete `Vec<Statement>` trees. `register_map` at line56 holds shared register locals; line179 adds the synthetic entry block. Typed/source-binding evidence is keyed to lifted statement positions (lines187–193, 201–213).
* `cfg/src/ssa/construct.rs:1222–1295` walks those trees again, saves original write operands, resolves reads, mints SSA definitions, and rewrites every slot. Recursive closure assignment deliberately publishes its write before reading captures (lines1231–1254); ordinary parallel writes read first.
* Construction then applies aliases, groups capture cells, propagates copies, applies aliases again, removes block parameters, and applies aliases a third time (lines1388–1402). These operations already have specialized visitors/buffers; another visitor conversion is not the proposed work.
* `cfg/src/ssa/inline.rs:967–979` reconstructs global read counts on each public invocation. Each block visit reconstructs a facts cache, producer index, and eligible-read snapshot (lines332–341), then scans backward across possible movement barriers (lines352–395). A successful substitution moves the expression, reduces the same roots, and restarts the consumer. Facts are intentionally scoped to one block visit (`inline/facts.rs:1–5`).
* `luau-lifter/src/lib.rs:1568–1634` invokes this pipeline inside ordered jump/inline/conditional/parameter rounds. The current code already caches dominators until topology changes and specializes terminal functions. A new generic dirty-block queue is not a new architectural solution.

### Alternative and exact boundary

Decode each operation into stable `OpId`/`ValueId` records with contiguous operand/edge lists and PC evidence; do not allocate one AST Box for each IR node. Register identity and captured-cell identity remain separate. Maintain ordered use occurrences and def links as operations are transformed. Use the same DFS, late-seal schedule, phi creation, copy propagation, source-binding and capture grouping rules first. This deliberately does **not** reproduce W9's early sealing.

An expression occurrence can be transferred by changing an operand ID, retaining its existing operation/metadata record. Eliminated assignment shells no longer force large Statement slots, RcLocal-containing operand vectors, and subsequent generic AST walks. Materialize the public AST only at the chosen boundary after SSA cleanup; retain the existing Destructor and structurer initially. Complicated instructions can initially use a lossless opaque payload, with their cost counted rather than hidden. This keeps the first backend comparison bounded while allowing a future extension through destruction.

The use-def index must retain occurrence order and duplicate reads, not just a set. It is insufficient to jump directly to a use: the same effects/errors, group writes, conditional positions, global lookup ordering and FASTPCALL late callee rules must still be checked. A movement/evaluation recipe must model these facts, including opaque calls and table-key errors. Preserve the existing eligible-read snapshot (inline.rs724–736), intentionally stale usage semantics inside a round, all inline/dead/table phase boundaries, every root reduction point, and rewrite budget accounting. Reduce is not idempotent; do not fuse or defer it casually.

A useful proof route is a shadow adapter that materializes the compact state at each existing phase boundary and compares it to the old pipeline, including local groups and metadata. During the first port, keep logical ID creation order and all legitimate definitions/phis; never introduce fake lineage records merely to reproduce hash order. Source-only and provenance-enabled builds must use the same algorithm and emit the same source. Preserve closure body publication and actual Arc handles at the public boundary, and establish owner-count equivalence before any owner-sensitive naming/reconstruction pass.

### Exposure and falsifiable hypothesis

W8 sees 26,391 function instances, 142,577 initial CFG blocks and 1,021,632 lifted statements, versus 86,601 blocks and 244,625 statements after cleanup. The 76.1% reduction in statement count is **not** 76.1% discarded expression work: W11 records 609,738 accepted substitutions, which commonly move retained RHS trees into consumers. The opportunity is avoiding transient statement/local transport and repeated analysis, not deleting those expressions.

W8 constructor counts include 1,196,400 read operands, 799,421 write operands and 1,342,559 definition records. W11 observes 62,303 inliner calls over26,391 functions, 1,847,490 statement visits, 1,525,197 fact builds, 4,154,234 search Pre/Post callbacks, 2,356,999 conditional-walk entries and 3,165,601 late-callee-walk entries. These are overlapping axes and cannot be summed into a work saving. They motivate explicit operation/use records spanning the phase rather than one more tree cache.

Falsifiable hypothesis: an implementation that preserves the old rewrite sequence but avoids materializing temporary register AST shells, and maintains their exact operands/facts during transfers, removes enough repeated construction/traversal to improve distinct-input ordinary runtime materially. Reject it if porting exact reductions/proofs requires repeatedly rematerializing consumers, if full AST adapters merely add another representation, or if ordinary runtime/RSS regresses as W12 did. Existing census does not give the eligible fraction for a partial opcode backend, so no admission percentage is asserted.

The smallest direct-SSA-only emitter is not sufficient: it removes at most lifting plus rename work, leaves inlining/destruction/region work intact, and must contend with reverse-PC lifting versus DFS SSA order and per-function ID bases (`lib.rs:513–555`). Do not change ID allocation/publication order as an accidental side effect of fusion.

## 2. SSA-aware structuring, with edge copies delayed until emission

There is a real conversion boundary to reconsider:

* Destructor first lifts phi parameters into new parameter/edge transport locals and parallel assignments (`cfg/src/ssa/destruct.rs:1235–1265`, 1302–1335), and can split conditional predecessor edges specifically for readable output (1344 onward). It then computes liveness/def-use/interference, coalesces groups, removes edge arguments (738–765), applies a local map, and sequentializes copies (389–433).
* Immediately afterwards, `restructure/src/region.rs:1162–1222` rediscovers reachability, dominators, postdominators, liveness and loop shapes. Its liveness is already a worklist with parallel-copy semantics (1320–1397), not a naive whole-graph fixed point. It explicitly supports SSA-like edge arguments and rejects malformed transfers (1178–1210).

An SSA-aware region plan could preserve original edge transfers until lexical regions are fixed, lower only surviving merge assignments, and compute the graph/proof summaries once on that representation. This would avoid constructing/splitting some transport-only CFG that the region layer immediately reconstructs. However, simply skipping Destructor is unsound: the current loop recognizers, representative-local names, captured-cell aliases, source-binding compatibility and parallel-copy cycles depend on its result. The source comment at destruct.rs1344 shows edge splitting changes while/repeat readability, not just runtime semantics. Region's existing support for edge arguments is not proof that its loop recognizers accept every pre-destruction graph.

The first proof would need acyclic diamond transfers and loop-backedge cycles, loop results captured by reference, iterator exhaustion adapters, numeric/generic-for hidden registers, malformed duplicate destinations, and failing speculative structuring with local-ID rollback. The old accepted fallback and metadata/provenance modes must remain equivalent. A post-coalescing liveness set cannot be reused as a naive quotient of pre-coalescing SSA liveness without proving alias/kill and edge-copy behavior.

This is a second-choice research direction: it can remove a conversion boundary, but current timing exposure does not justify a claim that it is larger than the compact-IR opportunity. In W7, parameter lifting and sequentialization together are only about0.57% of diagnostic time; skipping just those is not meaningful. A useful implementation must remove a substantial part of destruction plus duplicate graph analysis, not merely postpone copy allocation.

## Ceilings and explicit rejections

These are illustrative Amdahl limits using one internally comparable W7 diagnostic profile (11.643s DECOMPILE), **not ordinary CPU timing or a W11 speed prediction**. Telemetry overhead and W10/W11 changes limit transferability. Nested times are not double-counted:

| Entire phase family made free (unrealistic) | Diagnostic share | Illustrative maximum |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| DESER_LIFT + SSA_RENAME | 9.00% | 1.10x |
| DESER_LIFT + whole SSA construction | 15.47% | 1.18x |
| Construction + inline + destruction | 30.47% | 1.44x |
| Destruction + region structuring | 16.32% | 1.20x |
| DESER_LIFT + entire FUNCTION pipeline | 56.88% | 2.32x |

A 3x result requires eliminating over66.7% of current runtime; even making the entire measured lifting/function family free would not reach it in this profile. Therefore a CFG-only project cannot honestly promise3x, and larger goals would require substantial later AST/presentation work elimination too.

Do not repeat: W9 early sealing (slower and source/provenance-mode mismatch); W7 single-terminal specialization (already present); the9.6% initial logical-single-body SSA ceiling; generic block dirty scheduling (only2,739/1,850,229 visits avoided); adaptive liveness alone (W8 0.199s diagnostic, no broad timing ceiling); or transferable Reduce certificates (W11 only1.220 dispatches/root,90.756% leaf/opaque). Producer indexing already exists. Neither a per-local hash-table substitution nor another enum-size model answers the broader work-elimination question.

Evidence: `wave7-phase-allocation-final-profile/report.json`, `wave8-ssa-linear-attribution.json`, `wave11-ssa-work-summary.json`, and `wave12-rvalue-timing/independent-decision.json`. No new measurement was produced for this note.


## Smallest premise-validation slice (requested follow-up; design only)

Use two independently selectable ordinary backends for **lifting through SSA construction only**, joining at the unchanged `cleanup_ssa` boundary. The alternative is a hybrid block store: a compact record for a single-local/single-RHS assignment (`destination`, owned existing `RValue`, exact origin/flags/statement-PC evidence), plus an unchanged `Statement` payload for every other form. Keep compact records in their own contiguous vector behind ordered operation slots; putting the large fallback Statement directly in the record enum would defeat the storage premise. Do not invent another expression arena yet. Start by routing existing assignment emission into this sink; continue using the existing register-handle creation, SSA algorithm, capture logic, source-binding policy and copy-propagation order. A read/write adapter exposes the same operand order from compact records, avoiding the pair of one-element Vec allocations and rediscovering their fields through a generic statement tree. Materialize survivors exactly once before existing SSA cleanup. Do not add boxes per compact record.

This requires a compact-aware constructor view, not a second SSA algorithm. `fresh_local`/`fresh_phi`, every old register handle, duplicate definition insertion, hash reserves and hash-visible iteration stay in their original sequence. Reverse-PC lifting and DFS rename remain distinct schedules. Recursive closures, parallel writes, CLOSE and loop markers stay on the lossless legacy path initially; the function itself must not be excluded merely because provenance is enabled. Both representations carry source PC/type/role evidence at unchanged logical statement positions. Before admitting the slice, audit every constructor helper for a full-Statement assumption or owner-count observation; use exact materialization fallback at that point, count it, and avoid keeping a duplicate shadow AST alive. Run oracle replays separately with restored initial Local metadata and ID base so extra reference counts cannot conceal a difference. At handoff, require equal source AST, metadata, local/capture groups and their iteration order, next ID, and surviving local/closure owners. Existing reducers are entirely unchanged after the handoff; there is no normality certificate, deferred reduction or new rewrite budget.

**The crucial falsifier:** the alternative must keep the compact form through the constructor's existing copy propagation/parameter cleanup, without reordering those passes. A packed record that survives to handoff eventually pays the old operand-Vec allocation. Thus this slice is useful only if enough shells disappear before materialization, or enough measured rename/traversal work is removed to pay for dispatch and handoff. The observed76.1% statement shrink is not the eligible count: much of it occurs in the unchanged inliner. It must not be used as a projected saving for this slice.

Minimum count schema in a separately gated diagnostic run: compact candidates/admissions; refusals by shape; packed records removed before handoff; records requiring early materialization; surviving records materialized at handoff; old operand-Vec allocations actually avoided versus deferred; read/write operand callbacks and clones removed; compact slot/payload capacity and peak bytes; handoff allocations/bytes and operation visits. Keep metadata flags and owners out of diagnostic storage. Record these per function, joined to existing phase keys, but no per-node rows. A count-only replay can establish eligibility and correctness; it cannot demonstrate speed.

Then one small balanced ordinary comparison must time the **whole original lifting+construction+handoff interval and complete distinct-input API**, with both algorithms source-pinned and the same accepted output/mode gates. The legacy backend has no packing tax. The alternative includes every fallback and handoff cost; do not time only its inner lookup loop. Reject if the handoff reconstructs nearly all deferred allocations without reducing measured work, if owner/metadata parity needs fake identities or disabling tracing, or if ordinary CPU/RSS is not convincingly better. A win validates only this slice, not the larger compact IR or3x target. A loss rejects this boundary/shell design; it does not logically disprove a fully compact expression backend, but provides no reason to spend hours extending it without new, concrete evidence.


### Existing data check for this handoff boundary

Checked the aggregate W7 allocation profile and W8 light census report without re-reading raw partitions. In **both** reports, `F_SSA_CONSTRUCT`, `SSA_RENAME`, `SSA_PROPAGATE_COPIES`, `SSA_CONSTRUCT_REMOVE_PARAMS`, and `SSA_APPLY_LOCAL_MAP` all have `node_samples = 0`, `node_samples_incomplete = 0`, and all before/after statement/value sums zero. Those zeros mean no node samples, not empty functions. The parameter-graph counters count graph candidates/builds, not surviving Assign shells. Existing telemetry therefore does not determine constructor-only materialization savings.

The W11 frozen layout hook is confirmed at `luau-lifter/src/lib.rs:1775–1782`, immediately **after Destructor::destruct**, whereas its input hook is before construction at1662–1669. It cannot estimate the proposed post-constructor handoff. The W8 after-cleanup classifier is also too late.

Source narrows the expected savings further: `construct.rs:967–1005` removes only plain single-local copies whose source and destination are outside incoming/passed capture groups and whose source bindings are compatible. Other single-assignment RHS payloads survive this pass; parameter cleanup mostly affects edge transfers. Thus the proposed shell-only slice is **not implementation-ready on existing evidence**: the available counts cannot show that enough eligible copies disappear before handoff. If root elects to investigate further, the first added information should be a bounded before/after count of these exact compact-shell candidates and constructor-elided copies, not a large IR rewrite or another broad census. Until that count exists, a fuller through-inliner compact backend remains an architectural possibility, not an evidence-backed next implementation.


## W13 copy-shell census decision — NO-GO for constructor-only handoff

The bounded diagnostic is complete and independently audited:3,978 accepted inputs,26,391 functions,1,106,751 telemetry rows, no drops or misnesting. All26,391 completed constructors report the full20-field conservation identity; summing the four small partition summaries reproduces the aggregate. Source, compiler/build features, rebuilt local artifacts and executable hashes are pinned in `wave13-copy-shell-decision.json`. Two focused tests and all-target compile passed. No raw-profile replay or new run was performed for this decision.

There are **769,343 input candidate assignments**, **6 unreachable candidates**, **56,170 approved copy removals**, and **713,167 post-constructor survivors**. Thus **92.6982% survive** to the proposed AST handoff. The upper buffer-incidence opportunity is112,352 buffers avoided versus1,426,334 merely deferred. Removed copies account for5,841,680 operand-capacity payload bytes; the6 pruned candidates add624, totaling **5,842,304 bytes** (5.842MB decimal) across the corpus. This excludes headers/rounding, and is not a peak-memory or CPU measure. The modeled7,190,528 occupied Statement slot bytes are also not proof of freed block capacity.

**Skip implementation of the constructor-only compact-shell backend.** Nearly all candidate buffer allocations would move to the handoff rather than disappear, while a new representation adds packing, fallback and conversion costs. The result is an exposure-based rejection, not a speed benchmark. It does not reject a compact representation retained through the inliner/destructor or a complete instruction/value IR; those have a different elimination boundary and remain unproven. Main production code stays on the accepted W11 implementation.
